assessment: In this work, the authors test, in an animal model, a vaccine booster incorporating three linked SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor binding domain sub-units containing mutations from Omicron sub-variant BA.1 as well as other variants. They demonstrate that this is more effective at boosting neutralizing immunity against Omicron sub-variants and other variants including Beta and Delta than the same vaccine design but incorporating ancestral SARS-CoV-2 spike. While vaccine manufacturers are currently racing to make boosters based on Omicron sub-variant sequences, the approach presented in this paper, which combines mutations in addition to those found on individual Omicron sub-variant sequences, may offer another perspective on how to boost previous vaccine immunity to tackle emerging variants.
